QASHANI:92:8-12/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:92:8-12/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:92:8-12/r5.claim: God guides people toward Himself through intellect, sense, rational and transmitted evidence, and the capacity to reason and see clearly.
QASHANI:92:8-12/r5.anchor: بنور العقل والحس والجمع بين الأدلة العقلية والسمعية

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r6.claim: Verses 11–14 admonish Quraysh that God guides through revelation but does not force acceptance; they alone benefit from accepting, while both worlds remain under His control.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r6.anchor: this world and the next are in the grasp of God

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r8.claim: God's guidance here is showing the path and granting people perception.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r8.anchor: إن علينا للهدى: التعريف بالسبيل ومنحهم الإدراك، كما قال تعالى:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says guidance to truth is incumbent on God through proofs and exposition of the laws.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r9.anchor: إن الإرشاد إلى الحق واجب علينا بنصب الدلائل وبيان الشرائع

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447#2/r2.claim: God is responsible for making guidance clear; al-Zajjaj and Qatada say He explains guidance against error, including lawful and forbidden things.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447#2/r2.anchor: {إن علينا للهدى} يعني البيان. قال الزجاج: علينا أن نبين طريق الهدى من طريق الضلال

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447#2/r3.speaker: الفراء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447#2/r3.claim: Al-Farra interprets it as God’s commitment to show the path to whoever chooses guidance, like the straight path in another verse.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447#2/r3.anchor: قال الفراء: يعني من سلك الهدى فعلى الله سبيله (1) كقوله تعالى: "وعلى الله قصد السبيل"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447#2/r4.claim: Another view includes both guidance and misguidance among God’s acts; guidance alone is named because context supplies its opposite, as another verse names heat but not cold.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447#2/r4.anchor: إن علينا للهدى والإضلال كقوله: "بيدك الخير" (آل عمران -26)

BAYDAWI-FULL:92:8-12/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:8-12/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:8-12/r5.claim: Guidance is incumbent on God through decree or wisdom, or God provides the way of guidance, as in 16:9.
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:8-12/r5.anchor: { إن علينا للهدى } للإرشاد إلى الحق بموجب قضائنا أو بمقتضى حكمتنا

BINTSHATI:v2p111/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p111/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p111/r1.claim: Huda means guidance to the straight path and usually contrasts with misguidance and disbelief; al-akhira and al-ula mean end and beginning, and in religious usage the afterlife and this world.
BINTSHATI:v2p111/r1.anchor: الهدى الإرشاد إلى الطريق المستقيم، وأكثر ما يجيء في القرآن الكريم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p448/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p448/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p448/r3.claim: God has graciously committed Himself to show the true path and establish clear proofs; no one has an entitlement over Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p448/r3.anchor: للهدى * } أي البيان للطريق الحق وإقامة الأدلة الواضحة على ذلك

NAHHAS:v5p241/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p241/r18.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p241/r18.claim: The lām is emphatic and attaches to al-hudā; its alif is omitted to prevent confusion with negative lā.
NAHHAS:v5p241/r18.anchor: لام توكيد دخلت على الهدى فحذفت الألف لئلا يشبه لا التي للنفي ولاتصال اللام بما بعدها

DURR-FULL:v8p536/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r5.claim: He said God undertakes to explain what is lawful and forbidden, obedience and disobedience.
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r5.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم وابن جرير عن قتادة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r1.claim: أنذرتكم may be understood as present despite past morphology, bringing the past close to the present like the conventional call that prayer has begun; this follows from God's undertaking to guide.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r1.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الفاء للتفريع المعنوي فيكون فعل ( أنذرتكم ) مرادا به الحال وإنما صيغ في صيغة المضي لتقريب زمان الماضي من الحال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r7.claim: God's guidance means showing all paths and granting understanding, as also stated at 16:9; people then acquire what is decreed for them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r7.anchor: ثم أخبر تعالى أن عليه هدى الناس جميعا، أي تعريفهم بالسبل كلها ومنحهم الإدراك،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r8.claim: This is not guidance into faith, since that would leave no unbeliever.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r8.anchor: وليست هذه الهداية بالإرشاد إلى الإيمان، ولو كان كذلك لم يوجد كافر.

JISHUMI:v10p7439/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7439/r1.speaker: أبي
JISHUMI:v10p7439/r1.claim: A report from the Prophet promises that reciters of Sūrat al-Layl will receive until contentment, be protected from hardship, and have ease made easy for them.
JISHUMI:v10p7439/r1.anchor: وعن أبي، عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: من قرأ سورة (والليل) أعطاه الله حتي يرضى

JISHUMI:v10p7439/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7439/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7439/r2.claim: Following the previous chapter's account of the believer and disbeliever and their outcomes, this chapter gives the same contrast again.
JISHUMI:v10p7439/r2.anchor: ولما تقدم في السورة المتقدمة بيان حال المؤمن والكافر، وما فعل بهما، أتبعه بمثل ذلك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p767#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p767#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p767#2/r1.claim: God undertakes guidance by setting out proofs and explaining religious laws.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p767#2/r1.anchor: الإرشاد إلى الحق واجب علينا بنصب الدلائل وبيان الشرائع

QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r5.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj reads God's commitment to guidance as making the distinction between guidance and error clear.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r5.anchor: إن علينا أن نبين طريق الهدى من طريق الضلالة

QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r6.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r6.claim: Qatada explains this clarification as God's making clear what is lawful and unlawful, obedience and disobedience.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r6.anchor: بيان حلاله وحرامه، وطاعته ومعصيته قاله قتادة.

QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r7.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r7.claim: Al-Farra says whoever follows guidance is on God's straight path, citing the declaration that the straight way belongs to God.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r7.anchor: وقال الفراء: من سلك الهدى فعلى الله سبيله لقوله:

QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r8.claim: Another reading includes both guidance and misguidance, with the latter left implicit as in verses attributing all dominion or good to God.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r8.anchor: وقيل: معناه إن علينا للهدى والإضلال، فترك الإضلال كقوله:

QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r9.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r9.claim: Al-Farra notes that the wording about protection from heat also encompasses protection from cold.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r9.anchor: وكما قال: سرابيل تقيكم الحر [النحل: 81] وهي تقي البرد عن الفراء أيضا.

QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r10.claim: A further interpretation takes the promise as God's responsibility to reward the person He guided.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r10.anchor: وقيل: أي إن علينا ثواب هداه الذي هديناه.

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.claim: The sura develops two antitheses: behavior and recompense for the saved and damned, first in verses 5–13 and then in verses 14–21.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.anchor: Es folgen zwei Antithesen (V. 5–13 und V. 14–21), welche die Verhaltensweisen und Jenseitsschicksale von Seligen und Verdammten miteinander kontrastieren

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r6.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r6.speaker: Neuwirth
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r6.claim: Neuwirth classifies verse 11 with the theological predication in verses 12–13 rather than with the preceding description of the wicked.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r6.anchor: anders Neuwirth, Studien, 229 und Neuwirth, Frühmekkanische Suren, 228

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r8.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r8.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r8.claim: God's self-predication separates the second and third stanzas and serves as a compositional hinge affirming divine power over both worlds and supporting the threats and promises; Cuypers sees it as the sura's center.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r8.anchor: Die göttliche Selbstprädikation V. 12.13 setzt das zweite und dritte Gesätz voneinander ab: Sie fungiert als eine kompositorische Fuge

TABATABAI:92:8-13/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:92:8-13/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:92:8-13/r4.claim: God's ownership of both the last and first life explains the prior facilitation or concisely announces it: He guides because guidance is His responsibility and no obstacle can prevent Him.
TABATABAI:92:8-13/r4.anchor: تعليل لما تقدم من حديث تيسيره لليسرى وللعسرى أو الإخبار به بأوجز بيان

TABATABAI:92:8-13/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:92:8-13/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:92:8-13/r5.claim: God created people to worship Him and made worship a straight path to Him, commanding it through His messengers.
TABATABAI:92:8-13/r5.anchor: أنه خلقهم ليعبدوه كما قال وما خلقت الجن والإنس إلا ليعبدون

TABATABAI:92:8-13/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:92:8-13/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:92:8-13/r6.claim: God has undertaken to show people His way—whether they follow it or leave it—through verses on the clear and crooked paths, truth, and the choice to be grateful or ungrateful.
TABATABAI:92:8-13/r6.anchor: قضى على نفسه أن يبين لهم سبيله ويهديهم إليه بمعنى إراءة الطريق

TABATABAI:92:1-21/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:92:1-21/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:92:1-21/r1.claim: Prophetic guidance is also permitted guidance toward the path, as in 42:52 and 12:108; the author refers to an earlier rational discussion of prophethood.
TABATABAI:92:1-21/r1.anchor: هذا في الهداية بمعنى إراءة الطريق وأما الهداية بمعنى الإيصال إلى المطلوب

TABATABAI:92:1-21/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:92:1-21/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:92:1-21/r5.claim: The Qur'an guides all but is healing and mercy for believers, while it only increases wrongdoers' loss.

TABATABAI:92:1-21#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:92:1-21#3/r4.speaker: الإمام الرضا
TABATABAI:92:1-21#3/r4.claim: The Imam says God guides whom He wills and misguides whom He wills, rejecting companions' claim that knowledge is acquired by reasoning; the report appeals to Banu Hashim's closeness and right to the matter.
TABATABAI:92:1-21#3/r4.anchor: عن أبي الحسن الرضا عليه السلام قال، قلت قول الله تبارك وتعالى

TABATABAI:92:1-21#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:92:1-21#3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:92:1-21#3/r5.claim: Guidance as bringing a person to the end belongs to God as Lord; misguidance also belongs to Him only as retributive withholding of mercy, not as initial misguidance.
TABATABAI:92:1-21#3/r5.anchor: وأما الإضلال والمراد به الإضلال على سبيل المجازاة دون الإضلال الابتدائي

TABRISI:92:5-15/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:92:5-15/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:92:5-15/r13.claim: God is responsible for clarifying the path of guidance; actual response to guidance remains with people.
TABRISI:92:5-15/r13.anchor: معناه أن علينا لبيان الهدى بالدلالة عليه فأما الاهتداء فإليكم

TABRISI:92:5-15/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:92:5-15/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:92:5-15/r14.claim: Al-Tabrisi argues that guidance must be God's duty as clarification, since the possibility of divine misguidance would otherwise undermine that duty.
TABRISI:92:5-15/r14.anchor: أخبر سبحانه أن الهدى واجب عليه ولو جاز الإضلال عليه لما وجب الهداية

TABRISI:92:5-15/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:92:5-15/r15.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:92:5-15/r15.claim: Qatada glosses guidance as explaining obedience and disobedience.
TABRISI:92:5-15/r15.anchor: قال قتادة: معناه أن علينا بيان الطاعة والمعصية

THALABI:v10p218/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p218/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p218/r5.claim: God undertakes to clarify truth from falsehood.
THALABI:v10p218/r5.anchor: إن علينا للهدى أي بيان الحق من الباطل

THALABI:v10p218/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p218/r6.speaker: الفراء
THALABI:v10p218/r6.claim: He explains that God's path is the way of whoever follows guidance, the straight road sought from God.
THALABI:v10p218/r6.anchor: وقال الفراء: يعني من سلك الهدى فعلى الله سبيله

THALABI:v10p218/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p218/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p218/r7.claim: Another interpretation makes God responsible for both guidance and leading astray, citing God's possession of good and the garments that protect from heat.
THALABI:v10p218/r7.anchor: وقيل: معناه: إن علينا للهدى والإضلال، كقوله: بيدك الخير وسرابيل تقيكم الحر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p377/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p377/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p377/r1.claim: The statement can mean that God undertakes to explain the path of guidance.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p377/r1.anchor: علينا أن نبين طريق الهدى بمعنى أن الله تعالى يتكفل ببيان طريق الهدى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p377/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p377/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p377/r2.claim: It can also mean that the path of guidance ultimately leads its traveler to God.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p377/r2.anchor: أن الهدى يوصل صاحبه إلى الله

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p377/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p377/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p377/r3.claim: Putting the predicate first restricts guidance to God: guidance from another source is rejected and does not reach Him.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p377/r3.anchor: التقديم في هذه الآية يفيد القصر.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p377/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p377/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p377/r4.claim: The alternative order would retain the basic meaning but would not exclude another source of guidance.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p377/r4.anchor: إن الهدى علينا يتضمن المعنى السابق لكنه لا ينفي كون جهة أخرى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p378/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p378/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p378/r1.claim: The emphatic particles answer widespread rejection: people contest God's guidance and claim to define it themselves; emphasis reinforces both exclusivity and the path's destination.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p378/r1.anchor: أكثر الناس يرفضون هذا الأمر لقوله تعالى:

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p378/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p378/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p378/r2.claim: Had the wording been “إن الهدى لعلينا,” it would stress that guidance leads to God but lose the restrictive claim that guidance comes only from Him.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p378/r2.anchor: هذا يؤكد المعنى الثاني ويؤدي إلى فوات معنى الحصر الأول.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p378/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p378/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p378/r3.claim: The guidance statement connects to diverse human endeavors: if people sought God's guidance, their striving would not diverge; the next righteous description exemplifies that guidance.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p378/r3.anchor: لأنه لو ابتغى الناس الهدى عند الله لما تشتت سعيهم

ELMALILI:92:12-21/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r1.claim: Guidance belongs to God: showing the right path and truth, sending messengers, revealing books, setting signs in the world, and inspiring hearts to distinguish good from evil.
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r1.anchor: Felâha çıkaran doğru yolu göstermek, hakk u savâbı beyan etmek, resul göndermek, kitap indirmek, âfâkta edille nasbetmek, enfüste kalblere iyiyi kötüyü ilham eylemek

ELMALILI:92:12-21/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r2.claim: People cannot produce guidance by themselves, though accepting it and walking the path of good is entrusted to their will.
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r2.anchor: Allah’ın hidâyeti olmayınca siz kendiliğinizden onu yapamazsınız, ona göre hidâyeti kabul ettirip de hakk u hayr yoluna gitmek de sizin meşiyyetinize mevdû‘bir keyfiyettir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.claim: Others say verses 5–19 were revealed about Abu Bakr; regardless of a specific occasion, the message and rulings are general.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.anchor: bazıları ise 5-19. âyetlerin (bk. Elmalılı, VIII, 5881), müşriklerin işkence ettiği köleleri satın alıp âzat ederek hürriyetlerine kavuşturan Hz. Ebû Bekir hakkında indiğini söylemişlerdir. Âyetler böyle bir özel olay üzerine gelmiş olsa da, hükümleri ve mesajları geneldir

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3441/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3441/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3441/r1.claim: Qatada says God undertakes to make guidance clear, explaining what He permits and forbids, and what obedience and disobedience are.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3441/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : ان علينا للهدى يقول : علي الله البيان بيان حلاله وحرامه وطاعته ومعصيته

IBNASHUR:92:12/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:12/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:12/r1.claim: This resumes verses 5–10 and assigns responsibility to those choosing wrongdoing: God has excused them by directing them toward good, while each inclination brings facilitation toward its corresponding path.

IBNASHUR:92:12/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:12/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:12/r2.claim: The inclination underlying choice is called acquisition by al-Ashʿarī, the servant's capacity by the Muʿtazilites, and compulsion by the determinists.

IBNASHUR:92:12/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:12/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:12/r3.claim: The emphatic inna and lām answer the thought that, if God wanted people to believe, He would compel them; the same objection is quoted elsewhere.
IBNASHUR:92:12/r3.anchor: يومىء إلى أن هذا كالجواب عما يجيش

IBNASHUR:92:12/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:12/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:12/r4.claim: The preposition ʿalā conveys obligation: God undertakes guidance as an act of grace and wisdom before holding people accountable.

IBNASHUR:92:12/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:12/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:12/r5.claim: God first created humans able to distinguish right and wrong, then sent messengers to clarify ambiguous matters and remind them of harms they may overlook.
IBNASHUR:92:12/r5.anchor: فهدى الله الإنسان بأن خلقه قابلاً للتمييز بين الصلاح والفساد ثم عزز ذلك بأن أرسل إليه رُسُلاً

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p388/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p388/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p388/r1.claim: The emphatic إن and lām answer disbelievers who imagine that, had God wanted faith, He would have compelled them; they use this excuse for idolatry.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p388/r1.anchor: وتأكيد الخبر ب { إن } ولام الابتداء يومىء إلى أن هذا كالجواب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p388/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p388/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p388/r2.claim: على with a noun and verbal meaning conveys obligation: God undertakes guidance by grace and wisdom, first creating moral discernment, then sending messengers to clarify, remind, and guide before reckoning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p388/r2.anchor: وحرف ( على ) إذا وقع بين اسم وما يدل على فعل يفيد معنى اللزوم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p151/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p151/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p151/r1.claim: Al-Zajjāj says that God undertakes to clarify the path of guidance and the path of error.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p151/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج المعنى إن علينا ان نبين طريق الهدى من طريق الضلالة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p421#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p421#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p421#2/r1.claim: Qatada explains God's commitment to guidance as making the lawful and unlawful clear.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p421#2/r1.anchor: قال قتادة: {إن علينا للهدى} أي: نبين الحلال والحرام.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p421#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p421#2/r2.speaker: غيره
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p421#2/r2.claim: Another interpretation says whoever follows the path of guidance reaches God, likening it to the straight path that belongs to God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p421#2/r2.anchor: وقال غيره: من سلك طريق الهدى وصل إلى الله. وجعله كقوله تعالى: {وعلى الله قصد السبيل} [النحل: 9] . حكاه ابن جرير.

FARRA:v3p271/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p271/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p271/r4.claim: “Guidance is upon Us” means whoever follows guidance has his way with God, comparable to God directing the straight path.
FARRA:v3p271/r4.anchor: من سلك الهدى فعلى الله سبيله، ومثله قوله: «وعلى الله قصد السبيل

FARRA:v3p271/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p271/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p271/r5.claim: The phrase may include both guidance and misguidance, with the latter omitted just as “garments protect you from heat” also implies cold.
FARRA:v3p271/r5.anchor:
ويقال: إن علينا للهدى والإضلال، فترك الإضلال كما قال:
«سرابيل تقيكم الحر

JISHUMI:v10p7444/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7444/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7444/r3.claim: Wealth cannot help at death or during punishment; the passage encourages giving and warns against hoarding.
JISHUMI:v10p7444/r3.anchor: أن المال لا ينفع عند الموت والعذاب

JISHUMI:v10p7444/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7444/r4.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v10p7444/r4.claim: When told that someone amassed wealth, al-Ḥasan asked whether he had amassed his lifespan; since he had not, the dead cannot use wealth.
JISHUMI:v10p7444/r4.anchor: فقال: وهل جمع عمره، قال: لا، قال: فما يصنع الأموات بالمال؟!

JISHUMI:v10p7444/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7444/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7444/r5.claim: God must establish proofs to explain obligations; since guidance is incumbent on Him, He cannot lead people astray from religion.
JISHUMI:v10p7444/r5.anchor: أن نصب الأدلة واجب عليه لبيان ما كلف

KASHSHAF:92:12/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:92:12/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:92:12/r1.claim: Guidance to the truth is God's responsibility through establishing proofs and explaining the revealed laws.
KASHSHAF:92:12/r1.anchor: إن الإرشاد إلى الحق واجب علينا بنصب الدلائل وبيان الشرائع

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r1.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r1.claim: He says God undertook to make the paths of guidance and error clear.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r2.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r2.claim: He interprets guidance as explaining what is lawful and unlawful.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r3.claim: A further possibility is that God undertakes the reward for the guidance He has given.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#13/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#13/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#13/r1.claim: God undertakes to guide to truth by erecting proofs and explaining revealed laws.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#13/r1.anchor: أن علينا الارشاد إلى الحق بنصب الدلائل وبيان الشرائع

QUTB-ZILAL:92:12/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:92:12/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:92:12/r1.claim: As a gracious act, God undertook to make guidance clear to human nature and awareness through messengers, revelations, and signs, leaving no one an excuse and wronging no one.
QUTB-ZILAL:92:12/r1.anchor: لقد كتب الله على نفسه - فضلا منه بعباده ورحمة - أن يبين الهدى لفطرة الناس ووعيهم

RAZI-FULL:v31p183#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p183#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p183#2/r1.claim: Wisdom required God to explain worship, distinguish obedience from sin, offer guidance and exhortation, and call people to worship for their benefit, mercy, and lasting bliss.
RAZI-FULL:v31p183#2/r1.anchor: أخبرهم أنه قد قضى ما عليه من البيان والدلالة

RAZI-FULL:v31p183#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p183#2/r2.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v31p183#2/r2.claim: The Muʿtazila argue that God excuses people and only commands what they can do, so He does not impose the impossible.
RAZI-FULL:v31p183#2/r2.anchor: أنه تعالى أباح الأعذار وما كلف المكلف إلا ما في وسعه

RAZI-FULL:v31p183#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p183#2/r3.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v31p183#2/r3.claim: They argue that 'upon Us' means a duty is incumbent upon God, and that guidance would be pointless if humans did not originate actions independently.
RAZI-FULL:v31p183#2/r3.anchor: أن كلمة على للوجوب ، فتدل على أنه قد يجب للعبد

RAZI-FULL:v31p183#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p183#2/r4.speaker: الواحدي عن الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v31p183#2/r4.claim: Al-Wahidi transmits al-Farra's reading 'guidance and misguidance,' with misguidance elided as in 'garments protect from heat,' which also implies cold; Ibn Abbas via ʿAta says God guides allies to obedience and bars enemies from it.
RAZI-FULL:v31p183#2/r4.anchor: وذكر الواحدي وجها آخر نقله عن الفراء فقال المعنى : إن علينا للهدى والإضلال

RAZI-FULL:v31p183#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p183#2/r5.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v31p183#2/r5.claim: The Muʿtazila reject that reading by citing the distinction that the straight path is God's charge but the crooked path is not from Him.
RAZI-FULL:v31p183#2/r5.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : هذا التأويل ساقط لقوله تعالى : { وعلى الله قصد السبيل

STUDYQURAN:92:12/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:12/r1.speaker: Ibn Kathīr; al-Qurṭubī; al-Ṭabarī
STUDYQURAN:92:12/r1.claim: Some understand God's guidance here as explaining what is lawful and prohibited.
STUDYQURAN:92:12/r1.anchor: Some understand this verse to mean, “We will explain what is lawful and what is prohibited”

STUDYQURAN:92:12/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:12/r2.speaker: Ibn Kathīr
STUDYQURAN:92:12/r2.claim: Another interpretation is that whoever follows guidance will reach God in the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:92:12/r2.anchor: Others take it to indicate that one who travels the path of guidance will reach God in the Hereafter

STUDYQURAN:92:12/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:12/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:92:12/r3.claim: The verse parallels the teaching that God alone has the role of showing the way.
STUDYQURAN:92:12/r3.anchor: It can also be likened to other verses that explain that it is God’s place to guide and no one else’s

TAB-FULL:v24p476/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p476/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p476/r1.claim: God undertakes to explain truth from falsehood and obedience from sin.
TAB-FULL:v24p476/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {إن علينا للهدى} [الليل: 12] يقول: على الله البيان، بيان حلاله وحرامه، وطاعته ومعصيته

TAB-FULL:v24p476/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p476/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p476/r2.claim: Qatāda says God is responsible for clear exposition of the lawful and forbidden, obedience and disobedience.
TAB-FULL:v24p476/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {إن علينا للهدى} [الليل: 12] يقول: على الله البيان، بيان حلاله وحرامه

TAB-FULL:v24p476/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p476/r3.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
TAB-FULL:v24p476/r3.claim: Some grammarians understand the wording to mean that whoever follows guidance is on God's path, comparing 16:9.
TAB-FULL:v24p476/r3.anchor: من سلك الهدى فعلى الله سبيله، ويقول وهو مثل قوله: {وعلى الله قصد السبيل} [النحل: 9]

TAB-FULL:v24p476/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p476/r4.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
TAB-FULL:v24p476/r4.claim: Some grammarians also say the phrase means that guidance and misguidance are both God's, comparing the use of heat for cold in 16:81.
TAB-FULL:v24p476/r4.anchor: إن علينا للهدى والإضلال، كما قال: {سرابيل تقيكم الحر} [النحل: 81] وهي تقي الحر والبرد

TABATABAI:92:13-16/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:92:13-16/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:92:13-16/r1.claim: God’s guidance can include both real, creative guidance and legislative guidance, as shown by the One who gives each thing its form and guides it, and by the revealed path offering choice.
TABATABAI:92:13-16/r1.anchor: يمكن أن يكون المراد به مطلق الهداية أعم من الهداية التكوينية الحقيقية والتشريعية الاعتبارية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p83/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p83/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p83/r2.claim: God is responsible for making the path of guidance distinct from the path of error.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p83/r2.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: أي إن علينا أن نبين طريق الهدى من طريق الضلال (¬4).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p83/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p83/r3.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p83/r3.claim: God makes clear what is lawful and unlawful, and what counts as obedience and disobedience.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p83/r3.anchor: وهو قول قتادة: أي على الله البيان: بيان حلاله، وحرامه، وطاعته، ومعصيته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p83/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p83/r4.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p83/r4.claim: Whoever follows guidance has a path leading to God, His reward, and His Garden; the wording resembles “God's is the directed way” in 16:9.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p83/r4.anchor: القول الثاني: إن المعنى يقول: من سلك الهدى فعلى الله سبيله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p83/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p83/r5.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p83/r5.claim: A further reading supplies “misguidance” alongside guidance, as “garments protect you from heat” in 16:81 also implies cold.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p83/r5.anchor: ذكر (¬3) ذلك الفراء (¬4)، وذكر قولا آخر، فقال: ويقال: إن علينا للهدى والإضلال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p83/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p83/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p83/r6.claim: In ʿAṭāʾ's report, God guides His friends to obedience and prevents His enemies from acting in obedience, thus also expressing misguidance.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p83/r6.anchor: وهذا معنى قول ابن عباس في رواية عطاء، قال: يريد أرشد أوليائي إلى العمل بطاعتي

WAHIDI-QT:92:12/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:92:12/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:92:12/r1.claim: God undertakes to clarify the path of guidance from the path of error.
WAHIDI-QT:92:12/r1.anchor: { إن علينا للهدى } أي إن علينا أن نبين طريق الهدى من طريق الضلال

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:12:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:12:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:12:anmerkung/r1.claim: For hadā and hudā, consult the note to 93:7.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:12:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Zu hadā bzw. hudā vgl. die Anmerkung zu 93:7.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:12/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:12/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:12/r1.claim: God is responsible for clarifying the paths of guidance and error, good and evil, by sending scripture and prophets.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:12/r1.anchor: Kitap indirmek ve peygamber göndermek suretiyle hidayet ve dalâlet yollarını, hayrı ve şerri açıklamak Allah’a aittir

ALUSI-FULL:v30p150/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150/r1.claim: The verse resumes the argument: given God's wise decree in creating people to worship, He must guide them by directing them to truth or explaining both guidance and error, and He has done so fully; it does not prove the Muʿtazilī claim that God is obligated to do what is best.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150/r1.anchor: أي إن علينا بموجب قضائنا المبني على الحكم البالغة حيث خلقنا الخلق للعبادة أي ندلهم ونرشدهم إلى الحق

ALUSI-FULL:v30p150/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150/r2.claim: An alternative says guidance is entrusted to God alone, like the statement that the Prophet cannot guide whom he loves; Alusi objects that making 'upon Us' mean 'entrusted to Us' departs from the apparent syntax.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150/r2.anchor: وقيل المراد أن الهدى موكول علينا لا على غيرنا كما قال سبحانه إنك لا تهدي من أحببت

ALUSI-FULL:v30p150/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150/r3.claim: Another gloss makes the phrase a promise that those following the guided path will reach God, as in the statement that the straight path belongs to Him; Alusi notes the same syntactic difficulty.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150/r3.anchor: ومثله ما قيل أن المراد أن علينا طريقة الهدى على معنى أن من سلك الطريقة المبينة بالهدى والإرشاد إليها يصل إلينا

TAB:92:12/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:12/r1.speaker: author
TAB:92:12/r1.claim: God undertakes to clarify truth from falsehood and obedience from disobedience.
TAB:92:12/r1.anchor: إن علينا لبيان الحق من الباطل

TAB:92:12/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:12/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB:92:12/r2.claim: Qatada says God is responsible for clarifying what is lawful and unlawful, obedience and disobedience.
TAB:92:12/r2.anchor: عن قتادة ،   قوله :  إن علينا للهدى يقول :  على الله البيان

TAB:92:12/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:12/r3.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
TAB:92:12/r3.claim: Some Arab grammarians read this as God's way being the path of whoever follows guidance, comparing it with the statement that the straight path is God's responsibility.
TAB:92:12/r3.anchor: وكان بعض أهل العربية يتأوله بمعنى :  أنه من سلك الهدى

TAB:92:12/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:12/r4.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
TAB:92:12/r4.claim: Some Arab grammarians also understand the wording to encompass guidance and misguidance, like a garment said to protect from heat while protecting from cold too.
TAB:92:12/r4.anchor: وقال :  يقال معناه :  إن علينا للهدى والإضلال

ABUHAYYAN:92:12/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:12/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:92:12/r1.claim: God's guidance means defining the path and granting people discernment.

ABUHAYYAN:92:12/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:12/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:92:12/r2.claim: He links this guidance to the statement that God's responsibility is to make the straight path clear.
ABUHAYYAN:92:12/r2.anchor: كما قال تعالى : { وعلَى الله قصد السبيل }

ABUHAYYAN:92:12/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:12/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:92:12/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says guiding people to truth is incumbent on God through establishing proofs and explaining the revealed laws.
ABUHAYYAN:92:12/r3.anchor: وقال الزمخشري : إن الإرشاد إلى الحق واجب علينا بنصب الدلائل وبيان الشرائع

ALUSI:92:12/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:12/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:12/r1.claim: This resumes and confirms what precedes: under His wise decree, having created people for worship, God guides them to truth or clarifies guidance and misguidance, which He has fully done.
ALUSI:92:12/r1.anchor: استئناف مقرر لما قبله أي إن علينا بموجب قضائنا المبني على الحكم البالغة

ALUSI:92:12/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:12/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:12/r2.claim: The verse does not establish the Muʿtazilite claim that guidance is something God is obligated to provide.
ALUSI:92:12/r2.anchor: فلا يتم الاستدلال بالآية على الوجوب عليه عز وجل بالمعنى الذي يزعمه المعتزلة

ALUSI:92:12/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:12/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:12/r3.claim: Another view means guidance is entrusted to God alone, citing that the Prophet cannot guide whom he loves; al-Alūsī objects that the implied verb entrusted makes the syntax unlikely.
ALUSI:92:12/r3.anchor: وقيل المراد أن الهدى موكول علينا لا على غيرنا

ALUSI:92:12/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:12/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:12/r4.claim: A further gloss is that the path of guidance is upon God: whoever follows the clarified way arrives at Him, by analogy to the straight path being upon God; al-Alūsī likewise finds this attachment unlikely.
ALUSI:92:12/r4.anchor: ما قيل أن المراد ثم أن علينا طريقة الهدى على معنى أن من سلك الطريقة المبينة بالهدى

BAGHAWI:92:12/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:12/r2.speaker: الزجاج وقتادة
BAGHAWI:92:12/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj and Qatada say God undertakes to clarify guidance and misguidance; Qatada specifies the lawful and forbidden.
BAGHAWI:92:12/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج : علينا أن نبين طريق الهدى من طريق الضلال ،   وهو قول قتادة ،   قال : على الله بيان حلاله وحرامه

BAGHAWI:92:12/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:12/r3.speaker: الفراء
BAGHAWI:92:12/r3.claim: Al-Farraʾ reads it as God's undertaking of the way for whoever follows guidance, comparing the verse that says the straight path belongs to God.
BAGHAWI:92:12/r3.anchor: قال الفراء : يعني من سلك الهدى فعلى الله سبيله ،   كقوله تعالى : { وعلى الله قصد السبيل }

BAGHAWI:92:12/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:12/r4.speaker: بعضهم
BAGHAWI:92:12/r4.claim: Another interpretation includes both guidance and misguidance under God's power, as in the statement that good is in God's hand.
BAGHAWI:92:12/r4.anchor: وقيل معناه : إن علينا للهدى والإضلال كقوله : { بيدك الخير }

BAYDAWI:92:12/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:92:12/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:92:12/r1.claim: God undertakes to guide people to truth by His decree or wisdom; alternatively, the phrase means that the path of guidance belongs to God, as in 16:9.
BAYDAWI:92:12/r1.anchor: للإرشاد إلى الحق بموجب قضائنا أو بمقتضى حكمتنا أو إن علينا طريقة الهدى

BIQAI:92:12/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:92:12/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:92:12/r1.claim: In reply to an obstinate person's question about why God does not guide everyone to good, God distinguishes what He graciously undertakes from what He does by sovereign power; no one has a right over Him.
BIQAI:92:12/r1.anchor: ما له لا ييسر الكل للحسنى

BIQAI:92:12/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:92:12/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:92:12/r2.claim: What God has undertaken is to make the true path clear and establish evident proofs of it.
BIQAI:92:12/r2.anchor: البيان للطريق الحق وإقامة الأدلة الواضحة على ذلك

DURR:92:12/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:12/r1.speaker: قتادة
DURR:92:12/r1.claim: Qatada says God undertakes to make guidance clear by explaining what He makes lawful and unlawful, and what constitutes obedience and disobedience.
DURR:92:12/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : { إن علينا للهدى } يقول : على الله البيان بيان حلاله وحرامه وطاعته ومعصيته

IBNATIYYA:92:12/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:92:12/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:92:12/r1.claim: God undertakes to show all people the paths and grant them perception; each person then earns what has been allotted to him.
IBNATIYYA:92:12/r1.anchor: ثم أخبر تعالى أن عليه هدى الناس جميعاً ،   أي تعريفهم بالسبل كلها ومنحهم الإدراك

IBNATIYYA:92:12/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:92:12/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:92:12/r2.claim: This guidance is not guidance into faith, since that reading would leave no unbelievers.
IBNATIYYA:92:12/r2.anchor: وليست هذه الهداية بالإرشاد إلى الإيمان ،   ولو كان كذلك لم يوجد كافر

IBNATIYYA:92:12/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:92:12/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:92:12/r3.claim: He links God's guidance to the statement that the straight way is God's responsibility in 16:9.
IBNATIYYA:92:12/r3.anchor: كما قال تعالى : { وعلى الله قصد السبيل }

IBNKATHIR:92:12/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:92:12/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR:92:12/r1.claim: Qatada says God undertakes to make the lawful and unlawful clear.
IBNKATHIR:92:12/r1.anchor: قال قتادة : { إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا لَلْهُدَى } أي : نبين الحلال والحرام

IBNKATHIR:92:12/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:92:12/r2.speaker: غيره، حكاه ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR:92:12/r2.claim: Another interpretation says whoever follows the path of guidance reaches God, likening it to 16:9.
IBNKATHIR:92:12/r2.anchor: وقال غيره : من سلك طريق الهدى وصل إلى الله . وجعله كقوله تعالى : { وَعَلَى اللَّهِ قَصْدَ السَّبِيلِ }

MAWARDI:92:12/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:92:12/r1.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI:92:12/r1.claim: God's guidance means making clear the paths of guidance and misguidance.
MAWARDI:92:12/r1.anchor: أن نبين سبل الهدى والضلالة قاله يحيى بن سلام

MAWARDI:92:12/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:92:12/r2.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI:92:12/r2.claim: Qatāda interprets it as explaining what is lawful and unlawful.
MAWARDI:92:12/r2.anchor: الثاني : بيان الحلال والحرام ،   قاله قتادة

MAWARDI:92:12/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:92:12/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI:92:12/r3.claim: Māwardī also suggests that God undertakes the reward for the guidance He has given.

NASAFI:92:12/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:92:12/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:92:12/r1.claim: God undertakes to guide by setting out proofs and explaining the revealed laws.
NASAFI:92:12/r1.anchor: إن علينا الإرشاد إلى الحق بنصب الدلائل وبيان الشرائع

QURTUBI:92:12/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:12/r1.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI:92:12/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj says guidance here means making the path of guidance distinct from the path of error, that is, clarifying the rulings.
QURTUBI:92:12/r1.anchor: فالهدى : بمعنى بيان الأحكام ، قاله الزجاج

QURTUBI:92:12/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:12/r2.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI:92:12/r2.claim: Qatada specifies that God clarifies what is lawful and forbidden, and what constitutes obedience and disobedience.
QURTUBI:92:12/r2.anchor: بيان حلال وحرامه ، وطاعته ومعصيته . قاله قتادة

QURTUBI:92:12/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:12/r3.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI:92:12/r3.claim: Al-Farra says that whoever follows guidance is on God's path, citing the verse that God's responsibility is the directed path.
QURTUBI:92:12/r3.anchor: وقال الفراء : من سلك الهدى فعلى اللّه سبيله

QURTUBI:92:12/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:12/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI:92:12/r4.claim: One reading includes both guidance and misguidance, with the latter omitted, as in verses that mention one side while implying its counterpart.
QURTUBI:92:12/r4.anchor: وقيل : معناه إن علينا للهدى والإضلال ، فترك الإضلال

QURTUBI:92:12/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:12/r5.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:92:12/r5.claim: Another explanation is that God undertakes the reward of the guidance He has given.
QURTUBI:92:12/r5.anchor: وقيل : أي إن علينا ثواب هداه الذي هديناه

RAZI:92:12/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:12/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:92:12/r1.claim: After explaining the different outcomes of people's efforts, God states that He provided clarification, guidance, encouragement, and warning.
RAZI:92:12/r1.anchor: لما عرفهم أن سعيهم شتى في العواقب وبين ما للمحسن من اليسرى وللمسيء من العسرى ، أخبرهم أنه قد قضى ما عليه من البيان

RAZI:92:12/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:12/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:92:12/r2.claim: Since God created people for worship, wisdom requires explaining worship and distinguishing obedience from disobedience; He has done what wisdom requires to benefit and show mercy to them.
RAZI:92:12/r2.anchor: الذي يجب علينا في الحكمة إذا خلقنا الخلق للعبادة أن نبين لهم وجوه التعبد وشرح ما يكون المتعبد به مطيعا

RAZI:92:12/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:12/r3.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI:92:12/r3.claim: The Mu'tazilites infer that God grants excuses and charges only within capacity, so He does not impose the impossible.
RAZI:92:12/r3.anchor: ( إحداها ) : أنه تعالى أباح الأعذار وما كلف المكلف إلا ما في وسعه وطاقته

RAZI:92:12/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:12/r4.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI:92:12/r4.claim: They argue that ʿalā denotes obligation, implying something may be owed by God to a servant.
RAZI:92:12/r4.anchor: ( وثانيها ) : أن كلمة على للوجوب ، فتدل على أنه قد يجب للعبد على الله شيء

RAZI:92:12/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:12/r5.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI:92:12/r5.claim: They argue that if a servant did not independently bring actions into existence, establishing proofs would have no point.
RAZI:92:12/r5.anchor: ( وثالثها ) : أنه لو لم يكن العبد مستقلا بالإيجاد لما كان في وضع الدلائل فائدة

RAZI:92:12/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:12/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:92:12/r6.claim: Al-Razi says his school's replies to these Mu'tazilite arguments are well known, without detailing them here.
RAZI:92:12/r6.anchor: وأجوبة أصحابنا عن مثل هذه الوجوه مشهورة

RAZI:92:12/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:12/r7.speaker: الفراء
RAZI:92:12/r7.claim: Al-Farrāʾ, cited by al-Wāḥidī, reads guidance and misguidance as both being upon God, with misguidance omitted as in the phrase about garments protecting from heat.
RAZI:92:12/r7.anchor: وذكر الواحدي وجها آخر نقله عن الفراء فقال المعنى : إن علينا للهدى والإضلال ، فترك الإضلال كما قال : { سرابيل تقيكم الحر }

RAZI:92:12/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:12/r8.speaker: ابن عباس عن عطاء
RAZI:92:12/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, through ʿAṭāʾ, says God guides His friends to obey Him and prevents His enemies from obeying Him.
RAZI:92:12/r8.anchor: وهذا معنى قول ابن عباس في رواية عطاء ، قال : يريد أرشد أوليائي إلى العمل بطاعتي

RAZI:92:12/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:12/r9.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI:92:12/r9.claim: The Mu'tazilites reject al-Farrāʾ's reading: the straight way is upon God, while crooked paths are not from Him.
RAZI:92:12/r9.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : هذا التأويل ساقط لقوله تعالى : { وعلى الله قصد السبيل ومنها جائر } فبين أن قصد السبيل على الله
